title: DRAFT (deadend) — Retrocausal Task-Origin Stabilization (RTOS)
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
RTOS is a suspended draft exploring whether later user corrections can clarify an earlier task that was real but incompletely articulated. It distinguishes contemporaneous DSL from retrospectively stabilized DSL and sketches a score based on confirmation, correction, persistence, reduced task entropy, and a penalty for model-led drift.

The document’s real content is its prohibition. Only later user input may clarify task origin; a model cannot redirect the dialogue and then use the redirected conversation as evidence that its own frame was the task all along. Lead–lag precedence must classify whether the later frame was user-led or output-led. The proposed operator may not be deposited until it passes an adversarial case in which a genuine model redirect is followed by user pursuit and the operator still refuses retroactive legitimation.

No such successful break-test is reported. The title marks the branch as a dead end, the author register is unassigned, and the body says it is separate from the deposited DSL specification. The archive should preserve it as a documented danger and unrealized conjecture, not an operative metric.

wiki_article:
**Retrocausal Task-Origin Stabilization** is an abandoned or suspended methodological draft by Lee Sharks.

The draft considers whether later user corrections can reveal what an earlier, incompletely stated task was. It proposes comparing the score available at the time with a retrospective score after the task becomes clearer.

The proposed guardrail forbids a model from treating a frame it introduced as the user’s original intention. Only user-led confirmation, correction, or persistence may stabilize task origin, and lead–lag order must distinguish clarification from model-led drift.

The draft reports no successful adversarial test and explicitly says not to deposit or adopt the operator until it passes one. It is preserved as a dead-end record and warning about retrospective laundering.

modifications.was: Task-origin is often not fully present in the first input. The user frequently discovers the precise task through response, correction, and friction. So origin is both a prior constraint and a retroactively clarified event: real, but recognized late — not invented late.
